name: fact_picker
written: 2026-11-11 evening ET, before tools/fact_picker.py was run on any week (live or past)
why: operator 11/11: 'build the fact-sheet picker with the free data'. The headline-only picker (auto_picker) gives the agents no valuation, financials, performance, risk or technicals. Its 12-week replay showed no sign of skill at one month, and keeping only the names both agents picked did not help. This asks one new question: do the same two agents pick better for the next one to two months when each name comes with a fact sheet?
what_runs: tools/fact_picker.py run, Mondays 08:45 ET on the mini (com.jambi.fact-picker). No orders are placed. The auto_picker ledgers and their rules are not touched.
pool: symbols on the frozen list (docs/studies/pick_ledger_universe.txt) named in the past 7 days' headlines (the same headline pull as auto_picker), that have at least 252 daily bars and SEC revenue, net income and share-count facts filed before the run. If more than 100 qualify, the 100 named in the most headlines (ties alphabetical).
fact_sheet: one line per name, all known before the run: prices through the prior close (Alpaca daily, adjusted); SEC XBRL company facts with a filing date before the run date. VALUATION: market value, price/earnings, price/sales, price/book (trailing twelve months). FINANCIALS: revenue growth vs the same period a year earlier, net margin, operating cash flow / net income, debt (liabilities) / equity. PERFORMANCE: 1, 3, 6, 12-month return and 3-month return minus SPY. RISK: 60-day annualized volatility, 1-year worst drawdown, 1-year beta. TECHNICALS: price vs 50- and 200-day average, 14-day RSI, distance below the 52-week high. Plus up to 2 of the week's headlines for the name. A figure that cannot be computed is shown as n/a, never guessed.
not_included: analyst price targets and earnings estimates: no free source. The agents are told not to supply them from memory.
ask: each agent (AGY and Grok, same models and no-tool settings as auto_picker) gets the same sheet and returns a 0-100 score for EVERY name: its expected return relative to the S&P 500 over the next one to two months.
combine: combined score = mean of the two agents' scores, over names both scored. If either agent returns fewer than half the names, nothing is recorded that week. PICKS = the 3 highest combined scores not picked in the past 92 days (ties alphabetical) -> ledger ~/pick_ledgers/facts. Shadow ledgers, same rules: AVOID = the 3 lowest combined scores -> ~/pick_ledgers/facts_avoid; RANDOM = 3 names drawn from the same pool, seeded by the date -> ~/pick_ledgers/facts_random.
scoring: tools/pick_ledger.py rules unchanged: entry at the next open, ratio lift vs SPY, 30 random control names per pick, rank among them, beta-adjusted excess, t clustered by entry month.
verdict: ONE read, on the first 30 picks of the facts ledger, when all 30 have a closed 21-session window (about 10 weeks of picks plus a month). PASS = every pick_ledger pass condition at 21 sessions with t >= 2.0 (mean and median vs SPY > 0, more than half ahead of SPY, mean vs random names > 0, mean rank above the 50th percentile, beta-adjusted > 0) AND a mean vs SPY above the RANDOM ledger's over the same weeks. Anything else = FAIL. The 63-session figures are reported, not judged. AVOID is reported: if the avoid names trail the picks and the random names, that is noted as a lead for a later test, not a result.
replay: tools/fact_picker.py replay: the same twelve past Mondays as the auto_picker replay (2026-07-27 to 2026-10-12), sheets rebuilt as of each Monday (prices through the prior close, SEC facts by filing date), scored at 21 sessions. A SCREEN ONLY: the agents may have been trained on this period, adjusted prices carry later splits and dividends, and these twelve weeks were already looked at for the headline picker. A good replay does not change the live rule or shorten the live wait; a bad one does not stop the live run.
end: picks recorded after 2027-11-11 do not count (the ledger's own end date). No change to the prompt wording, the sheet or the combine rule while the live record runs; a change is a new test with a new ledger.
